requirement:
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`.

```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
    pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
}
```

Each span uses byte offsets into the supplied source snapshot, with an exclusive
end and boundaries valid for slicing that text. It includes the item's attached
source under the language's rules. The root has an empty selector and span
`0..source.len()`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. I did not request any implementation source.

- **Outline covers the whole retained file, even for a selected item:**
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` selects the third item of a file. It asserts that `selected.outline().items.len()` is 3, so the selected value still exposes the full outline, root included.
  - The same test checks that `selected.select("")` returns the retained root with the full text.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` asserts `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` for a selected section.
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts the same pointer equality for a selected function.
- **Root first, then items in source preorder:**
  - The Rust test asserts the exact selector sequence `["", "mod[auth]", "mod[auth]/fn[check]", "mod[auth]/struct[Token]", "fn[last]"]`. It also asserts the kinds `["", "mod", "fn", "struct", "fn"]`. Together these show the root first, parents before children, and children before the next top-level sibling.
  - The Markdown tests assert nested section order, including duplicate `#1` and `#2` siblings and the anonymous section and block items.
  - The plain-text tests assert line order.
- **Selectors identify items and ancestry:** this is delegated to the cited `selector_syntax`. The tests still use full nested selectors and select each item back through them.
- **Byte-offset spans with exclusive end and slicing-valid boundaries:**
  - `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` uses multibyte text (`é`, `🦀`). It asserts the exact spans `[0..source.len(), 0..2, 6..10]` and checks the sliced text.
  - Several tests assert `source.get(item.span.clone()).is_some()` for every item. `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` does this across all bundled languages.
  - The Rust and Markdown tests assert `selected.text() == &source[item.span]`.
- **Span includes attached source under the language's rules:**
  - The Rust test asserts that the function span starts at the doc comment `/// Check tokens.` and includes `#[inline]`, and that it ends at the end of the function.
  - The Setext tests assert that Markdown section spans start at the original heading text and retain container syntax.
- **Root has an empty selector and span `0..source.len()`:** asserted in the Rust, Markdown, Unicode, plain-text, and bundled-language tests. The empty-source case in `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` asserts the root span `0..0`.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

Each span uses byte offsets into the supplied source snapshot, with an exclusive
end and boundaries valid for slicing that text. It includes the item's attached

:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
